Base directory for this skill: /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/skills/jusprin-release

# Making a JusPrin release

`.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml` builds one commit into a draft
release. It refuses the commit without a new version, release notes, a guide
check and the Sentry secrets (see "Releasing" in `AGENTS.md`). It does not
run tests, check the server, check translations or audit error handling.
This skill covers all of it, in order.

## Kenneth decides these

Ask, and wait for his yes before each one. A yes covers that action only.

- The version, when he has not named it, and the release notes' wording.
- Deploying the server.
- Which error-handling findings must be fixed before the release.
- Taking in commits that landed on `jusprin-dev` after the range was fixed.
- Spending API money (say the cost).
- Every push, and moving `main`.
- Starting the release workflow.
- Downloading the draft's files.
- The Sentry values and read-only token for checking the draft.
- Posting anything on GitHub.

Never publish the draft: Kenneth does, by hand. Never force-push `main`.

## When something has to be fixed

A fix is its own commit on `jusprin-dev`, made in a worktree of its own from
`origin/jusprin-dev`, never in the release commit. Once it is pushed:

- **Before section 8 landed the release commit:** rebase your branch onto
  `origin/jusprin-dev`, record that as the new end of the range, and redo
  step 1.4 and sections 2 to 7.
- **After it landed:** keep the version. Redo step 1.4 and sections 2 to 7
  up to the fix, land what changed (section 8), move `main` and start the
  workflow again. A new run for the same version replaces the draft.

## Where each platform is tested

Every release is tested on all three platforms, twice: the test suites
(section 5) and the draft's own files (section 10). An untested platform
blocks the release.

- **macOS:** this computer.
- **Windows and Linux:** the two Google Cloud test VMs. How to reach, start,
  build on and run the app on each is in
  `<main checkout>/.claude/vm-harness/windows/README.md` and `…/linux/README.md`.
  That folder is local to this computer, never in the repository. Start a
  stopped VM, and stop it again when done. If a VM or that folder is
  missing, stop and tell Kenneth.

## 1. Set up

1. The main checkout (the folder holding `jusprin-dev`) must have no changed
   tracked files and no commits missing from `origin/jusprin-dev`. If it has
   any, list them for Kenneth and wait; never push, commit or discard them
   yourself. Untracked files are his working docs and do not block.
2. The range is the newest `jusprin/v*` tag to the current
   `origin/jusprin-dev`. Record that commit: every later step checks this
   range, and section 8 checks whether `jusprin-dev` moved.
3. Settle the version, then make a worktree at that commit under
   `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/`, on branch `claude/release-<version>` (add a
   suffix if taken). Never name a branch `jusprin-release/...`: pushing one
   starts an unsigned release build.
4. Read every commit in the range for what a person would notice and the
   GitHub issues it fixes.

## 2. Version and release notes

1. `kVersion` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp`.
2. `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md`, shaped like
   the previous one, for a person who prints. It becomes the draft's text on
   every workflow run, and an older app shows it under "Release notes" in
   Preferences › Updates. Check every on-screen label you quote against the
   source.
3. Anything new the app sends from the person's computer goes in the notes,
   with what it holds.

## 3. Server readiness

Every address the release calls must already answer on
`https://jusprinv2.obico.io`. Many are joined from pieces, so list them from
the code that builds them and write out each full path:

```bash
git grep -n -E '"/(ent|o|accounts|jusprin)/|"/models"|ask_server\("' -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin ':!*test*'
```

For example `ask_server("code/confirm", …)` is
`/ent/jusprin/v2/auth/code/confirm`, and the model list is the gateway's
address with its last part replaced by `/models`. A bare GET with no sign-in
or real data is enough: any 4xx answer except 404 means the address is there.

First GET a made-up address such as `/ent/jusprin/v2/no-such-address`: it
must answer 404. In maintenance mode the server answers 200 for every path,
and the check cannot tell anything apart; stop and tell Kenneth.

A missing address means the server change is not deployed. Find it in
tsd-enterprise (`web_ent/jusprin/v2/urls.py` on `master`) and tell Kenneth,
along with any other server behavior the range relies on. Deploying is his
call.

## 4. Error-handling audit

Run the `error-handling` skill on the range. When the release relies on
server changes, also audit tsd-enterprise's `web_ent/jusprin/` commits on
`master` since the previous tag's date (that repository has no release tags).
Report the findings and wait for Kenneth to say which must be fixed.

## 5. Tests

Build in your worktree in Release, following "Building on a shared machine"
in `AGENTS.md`. Use CMake.app's cmake (Homebrew's fails to find Eigen3), node
on `PATH`, and absolute paths.

The app builds against the main checkout's dependency folder, which may
predate a dependency the range added or changed. Bring it up to date first:

```bash
<worktree>/scripts/deps_current.sh <main checkout>/deps/build/arm64
```

It compares the `deps/` recipe the folder was last built from with the
worktree's, and when they differ it rebuilds the libraries that changed. If
it says the main checkout's recipe differs from the worktree's, the main
checkout is not at the end of the range; stop and tell Kenneth.

```bash
cmake -S <worktree> -B <worktree>/build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=<main checkout>/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
cmake --build <worktree>/build/arm64 --config Release --target tests/all jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs -- -j4
ctest --test-dir <worktree>/build/arm64/tests -C Release --output-on-failure -LE RequiresApp
```

`CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` takes one path only. `tests/all` builds every test
program, including `shell_integration_harness` for the guide check.
`agent_live_tests` is built but never registered with ctest, since each run
is billed. Also run `npm test` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI` and
`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI`.

- **Windows and Linux,** on the VMs, from a checkout of the end of the range:
  `build_win.bat -s --run-tests`, and `./build_linux.sh -st` then
  `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release --output-on-failure`, keeping the
  `RequiresApp` tests, which run only on Linux.
- **Prompt suites,** when the range changes text the model reads: run
  `tests/project_prompt` (and `tests/printer_prompt` when printer chats
  changed) on the free `claude-cli` backend. Its README also asks for a small
  paid run on the app's default model before a release; propose it with its
  cost.

To tell whether the range caused a failure, run the same test on a build of
the last release's tag. A failure there too is older: report it and let
Kenneth decide. One the range caused is a bug to fix before the release.

## 6. Translations

After the audit and tests, since a fix can add a sentence.

1. Run `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py` (needs GNU
   gettext and `npm ci` in `AgentUI`). Changed catalogs go in the release
   commit.
2. Translate new entries in JusPrin's own catalogs, `Localization/native/`
   and `Localization/pages/`, as `Localization/README.md` says. Never touch
   upstream's `localization/i18n/` or run `run_gettext`; from `AGENTS.md` and
   the `orca-translations` skill take only the editing rules and glossary.
3. `npx vitest run src/catalogs.test.ts` in `AgentUI` must pass.
4. Rebuild `jusprin_web` and `jusprin_catalogs` for the guide check.
5. Tell Kenneth how many entries are marked `# Needs human review`.

No tool finds a sentence nobody marked for translation; look for one while
reading the range.

## 7. Guide check

Follow "Before a release" in `docs/guide/README.md`, on the step 5 build.

1. Tell Kenneth first: it drives the app on this Mac's screen, and nobody
   should use the computer meanwhile.
2. Add new screens or menu items from the range to the guide before the
   check: it cannot find them, and a page changed after it passes is
   unchecked.
3. Run `<worktree>/scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai`. The script checks the
   tree it sits in, so the main checkout's copy checks the wrong code. It
   writes `docs/guide/checked-version.txt` when it passes.

## 8. Commit and land

1. The release commit holds `Version.hpp`, the notes, the catalogs, and what
   the guide check changed: `docs/guide/` (pages, `pictures/`,
   `checked-version.txt`) and `AgentUI/src/skills/guide-*/`. Nothing else.
2. If `origin/jusprin-dev` moved past the recorded end of the range, list the
   new commits for Kenneth. With his yes, rebase and redo step 1.4 and
   sections 2 to 7. If he says no, the release waits: your branch cannot
   reach `jusprin-dev` without them.
3. With his yes, push to `jusprin-dev` without a merge commit, then
   `git -C <main checkout> pull --ff-only`. If that pull is refused, stop and
   tell Kenneth without changing the main checkout.
4. With his yes, move `main` to that exact release commit, as a fast
   forward only.

## 9. Start the release workflow

The publisher is the repository variable `JUSPRIN_RELEASE_PUBLISHER`, or
`kennethjiang` when unset; `gh api user -q .login` must print it. This
computer's `gh` token cannot read repository variables or secrets (403), so
the workflow's first job is what reports a wrong publisher or a missing
Sentry secret (`JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN`, `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_URL`,
`SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT`). Only Kenneth can add a secret.

With his yes:

```bash
gh workflow run jusprin_release.yml --ref main -f sign_macos=true
```

Keep Mac signing on: Homebrew refuses an unsigned Mac app. Check that the new
`workflow_dispatch` run is on the release commit. If its "Upload to the draft
release" job waits for an approval (the `release` environment can require
one), tell Kenneth. A failed run is reported with its log, never worked
around with a skip box.

The Mac jobs build on GitHub's Macs. If GitHub has no Mac machine for the
repo, they end "cancelled" 15 minutes after they were queued, with no runner
and no steps. GitHub can also cancel a Mac job that is already building, for
lack of capacity: its log then ends with only "The operation was canceled".
Either way, tell Kenneth. With his yes, start the run again on Kenneth's own
Mac (the self-hosted runner, user `jusprin-ci`):

```bash
gh workflow run jusprin_release.yml --ref main -f sign_macos=true -f self_hosted_mac=true
```

## 10. Test the draft

Test the draft's own files: the Mac disk image on this computer, the Windows
installer and the AppImage on their VMs. Install over the previous release,
check that Preferences shows the new version, have one chat and slice, and
check each fix in the notes on the platform where it mattered. Kenneth signs
in, or you use a test account he names; never type a password. A chat spends
that account's credits.

Never print the app's settings file (the `.conf` file in its data folder), on
the VMs or here: it holds saved API keys and sign-ins, and whatever a command
prints stays in the session's log. Read or change the one setting you need,
such as the language, with a command that prints only that setting.

Sentry must be able to read this release's stacks. Kenneth gives you
`SENTRY_URL`, `SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT` and a read-only
`SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`; set them in the shell only, never in a file. From the
release worktree, on the Mac for the disk image and the unpacked Windows
portable zip (its `JusPrin/` folder), and on the Linux VM for the AppImage
(`--appimage-extract` only works on Linux; that VM needs a checkout of the
release commit and node):

- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_debug_files.sh verify <file>` on
  the Mac app's `Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer`, Windows' `OrcaSlicer.dll` and
  the AppImage's `squashfs-root/bin/orca-slicer` must print "Sentry holds
  debug information".
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_page_maps.sh verify <folder>` on
  the Mac app's `Contents/Resources`, the Windows zip's `JusPrin/resources`
  and `squashfs-root/resources` must say Sentry holds both pages' source
  maps.
- The app cannot cause an error report on purpose, and Help › Report a
  problem opens a GitHub issue, not a Sentry report. If an unexpected error
  happens while testing, send it and check in Sentry, under release
  `JusPrin <version> (OrcaSlicer <SoftFever_VERSION from version.inc>)`, that
  the app's frames show function, file and line. Otherwise say it was not
  done.

`winget_updater.yml`, inherited from OrcaSlicer, would submit the installer
to winget as `SoftFever.OrcaSlicer` on publish. `gh workflow list --all` must
show it `disabled_manually`; if not, tell Kenneth before he publishes.

Tell Kenneth what was tested on which platform. He publishes.

## 11. After publishing

- Start the previous release and check that Preferences › Updates offers the
  new one. The update check reads only published releases.
- With Kenneth's yes, reply to and close the issues the release fixes, and
  open a Homebrew cask pull request if JusPrin's cask is in Homebrew
  (`brew info --cask jusprin`).
- In Sentry, a new report's or crash's stack must name the app's functions
  with file and line, and a page error's frames the pages' sources
  (`AgentUI/src/...`, `HomeUI/src/...`). Bare addresses or
  `app:///home/index.html` positions mean a platform's debug files or a map
  are missing: run the verify scripts on that platform's released files.
- The next day, run the `jusprin-production-check` skill in tsd-enterprise.
- Remove your worktree and branch.

- **JusPrin in your language.** JusPrin's own screens, the AI chat and Home are translated into the 22 languages OrcaSlicer ships. Choose the language in Preferences › Appearance › Language. Numbers follow it too, for example "0,4 mm" in German. The translations are made by machine, so some wording may read oddly.
- **More printers connect from the printer chat.** The printer chat can now connect every connection type OrcaSlicer's printer settings offer, not only Klipper (Moonraker) and OctoPrint. This includes Elegoo Centauri Carbon and Centauri Carbon 2 printers (Elegoo Link). The chat cannot finish Repetier, UltiMaker, or PrusaLink with a user name and password, and tells you where to set those up instead. Obico, SimplyPrint and 3DPrinterOS still need their own sign-in.
- **Reporting errors.** When something goes wrong that you can't fix yourself, JusPrin shows one message, "Something went wrong on our side". You can see the whole report, then press Report to JusPrin team, or tick "From now on, report errors like this automatically". You can also turn this on or off in Preferences › Updates › Error reports. It is off until you turn it on.

## Fixed

- In languages that write decimals with a comma, such as German, French, Spanish, Portuguese and Russian, the add-printer form showed no nozzle sizes for most printers, so the printer could not be added. Bed sizes such as 233.5 mm were also read as 233 mm, and a 0.4 mm nozzle in an opened 3MF file was read as 0. This always happened on Windows.
- A calibration test started from one of your projects lost that project and its chat.
- A project could save itself again after sitting idle, with nothing changed.
- A file the AI chat refused to attach (too large, or a kind it can't read) stopped the project from saving until you removed it.
- If JusPrin couldn't write its settings file, signing in or saving an API key looked like it worked, and was lost when you quit. JusPrin now shows an error instead.
- Deleting your account now waits until AI has finished replying in any chat.
- A chat whose account or API key was removed showed the wrong model in its greyed-out model picker. It now shows the model the chat ran on.
- When AI prepared a print, it could keep checking the slice it had just started, again and again, while the slice ran.

## What JusPrin now sends

- **When the app starts**, it tells JusPrin's server once that it started: a random number made on the first start, the app's version and the name of your operating system. Nothing in it names you, and no sign-in goes with it. It is not sent in stealth mode.
- **Error reports and crashes** go to JusPrin's error tracker (Sentry) only when you press Report to JusPrin team, or when you have turned on automatic reports. A report holds where in the app the error happened, the steps just before it (never what you typed or what AI said), your operating system and the app's log for that run. A crash report also holds the app's state at the moment it crashed. With automatic reports off, a crash report stays on your computer.

JusPrin 2.0.2 can run its AI chats on a model on your own computer, lets AI add holes and parts to your models, and tells you clearly what to do when your own AI account refuses a request.

## New

- **AI on your own computer.** Chats can run on a model in Ollama or LM Studio, with no account and no credits. Set it up in Preferences › BYOAI › A model on this computer: press Find models, pick one, and press Use this model. JusPrin checks that the model can use the app's tools and has a context of at least 32k. It then shows under "On this computer" in each chat's model menu. Web search is not available for these chats, and a model that cannot see pictures is sent none.
- **AI can add holes and parts.** Ask AI for a screw hole, a slot, a peg or a lip, and it adds boxes or cylinders to your object, as solid parts or as holes. One Undo removes them. Asked for text or a logo, AI gives you the steps to add it yourself; a logo must be an SVG file.
- **AI can change your printer's hardware settings,** such as the bed size, the nozzle and the number of extruders. Before, it told you to change them by hand.
- **More printers connect from the printer chat.** For a Flashforge printer in LAN Only mode, PrusaLink with a user name and password, or Repetier, the chat opens a form that asks for the serial number, access code, login or printer name. What you type goes only to the printer; AI does not see it. Only UltiMaker still has to be set up in the printer settings window.
- **Home tells you when a new version is out.** A card at the top of Home's right column says which version is available. See what's new shows the release notes, Open download page opens the download page, and you can choose Remind me tomorrow or Skip this version.
- **OrcaSlicer's message boxes go into the chat.** In the JusPrin view, messages such as a failed printer connection or a refused print job now show in the project's chat instead of in a box over the app. Switching printer, filament or process while settings are changed no longer asks "Transfer or discard changes": JusPrin saves a version of the project first, so Version history keeps your changes, and the chat says which profiles the settings now follow.
- **Clearer messages when your own AI account refuses.** With your own key for OpenAI, OpenRouter or Anthropic, JusPrin now says when the account is out of credits, when the key is not allowed, or when the chat is too long for the model. When the service explains a refusal itself, JusPrin shows its words, for example "OpenRouter says: …". When the service is down or overloaded, JusPrin says it could not reach the service, instead of "Something went wrong on our side".
- **About 200 more sentences are translated,** including the titles of AI's actions in the chat, setting values in the Changes list, and the printer chat's first message.

## Fixed

- On Windows, quitting JusPrin crashed when error reports were turned on.
- On Windows in German and other languages, Ask AI about filament settings opened an empty chat with "Something went wrong on our side".
- On Windows in French, Spanish or Portuguese, a chat whose title had an accented letter, such as "Problème", failed to send.
- A chat whose reply stopped during a web search could not be continued: every next message failed.
- When AI switched to another printer with more filaments than that printer takes, the printer was switched and then the setup failed half done. It is now refused before anything changes.
- AI could end a chat with "cannot run (invalid_arguments)" after writing a note that was too long. It is now told which text was too long and the limit, and shortens it.
- Import printers from OrcaSlicer stayed on "Importing…" with every button greyed out after Cancel on the unsaved-changes question.
- On Linux with Wayland and an Intel graphics card, the Preview, Device and Project tabs could freeze.
- On Windows, when the 3D view could not start OpenGL, JusPrin could crash or show an empty 3D view. It now says which graphics card it found and what to check.
- In Preferences › BYOAI, when connecting an outside AI app such as Claude Code failed, the message gave no next step. It now says to copy the command and run it yourself, with a Copy button.
- Many messages written for AI were shown to you instead, such as "A hello handshake is required". Typing a message and then opening an earlier chat lost what you typed. Resume on an earlier chat failed after a slice. "Revert to here" opened a "Revert failed" window, and pressing the slice button twice opened "Couldn't slice".
- A photo in HEIC format renamed to .jpg is now refused when you attach it, instead of failing the chat.
- A project whose chats were saved by a newer JusPrin now says so in the chat, instead of showing no chats.

## What JusPrin now sends

- **Error reports and crashes** now carry your JusPrin account number when you are signed in, or else the random number this install made on its first start, so we can tell how many people a problem hits. Your email is not sent. Reports are still sent only when you press Report to JusPrin team, or when you have turned on automatic reports.
- **A chat on a model on your computer** is sent only to the address you entered in Preferences, not to JusPrin or any AI service.

## Downloads

- **Windows (64-bit):** the installer, or the portable .zip, which runs without installing.
- **Mac:** one disk image for Macs with Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
- **Linux (64-bit):** an AppImage, built on Ubuntu 24.04. Make the file executable, then run it.
- **SHA256SUMS.txt** lists each file's checksum.

Questions or problems: write to jusprin-support@obico.io, or use Help › Report a problem in the app.

# JusPrin Linux GUI test VM

A GCP VM for building JusPrin on Linux and testing its GUI, either by hand over
remote desktop or by script on a headless display.

| | |
|---|---|
| Instance | `jusprin-linux-test`, project `elegoo-backend`, zone `us-west2-a` (Los Angeles, for low latency from California) |
| Machine | n2-standard-16 (16 vCPU, 64 GB), 300 GB pd-balanced, no GPU |
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, XFCE desktop |
| Toolchain | Ubuntu's gcc 13, CMake 4.3.0 (same as the CI runner, in /opt), Node 24.11.1 (in /opt) |
| Checkout | `~/JusPrin` on branch `jusprin-dev` (user `kenneth`) |
| OpenGL | Mesa llvmpipe, OpenGL 4.5 core, software rendering |

The VM has no service account, so it cannot call GCP APIs. It cannot fetch the
private GitHub repo either; send commits with a git bundle (below).

## Scripts (run on the Mac)

- `./vmssh.sh '<command>'` runs a command on the VM.
- `./vmscp.sh <src> <dst>` copies files; write `VM:~/path` for the VM side.
- `./connect-rdp.sh` starts the VM if stopped, prints the login, and holds an SSH
  tunnel open. Point Windows App (Microsoft Remote Desktop) at `localhost:33890`,
  user `kenneth`. xrdp listens only on the VM's own localhost, so the project-wide
  `default-allow-rdp` firewall rule does not expose it.
- `env.sh` holds the instance name and forces the `ai-agent` service account. It
  also points gcloud at uv's standalone Python 3.12, because Homebrew's Python lost
  its OpenSSL library when Homebrew moved from openssl@3 to openssl@4.

## Scripts (copied to the VM's home folder)

- `~/vm-run-app.sh [args]` starts the built app on headless display `:99` (Xvfb
  with the xfwm4 window manager) with data dir `~/jusprin-test-data`. Log:
  `~/app.log`. It sets `SSL_CERT_FILE`; without it OrcaSlicer's Linux build stops
  at startup on a dialog asking which certificate file to use.
- `~/vm-screenshot.sh` saves display `:99` to `~/shot.png`.
- Click with `DISPLAY=:99 xdotool mousemove X Y click 1`. Screenshot pixels equal
  screen coordinates (1920x1080).
- Stop the app with `pkill -x orca-slicer`. Never `pkill -f orca-slicer` over
  ssh: it matches the ssh command's own text and kills the session.

## Build

```bash
# First time on a fresh VM: deps (about 25 min) then app and tests (about 30 min)
cd ~/JusPrin && ./build_linux.sh -dst -j 16
# After code changes: app and tests only
cd ~/JusPrin && ./build_linux.sh -st -j 16
```

The app lands in `~/JusPrin/build/package/bin/orca-slicer`. Run long builds
detached so an ssh disconnect does not kill them:

```bash
setsid nohup bash -c 'set -o pipefail; ./build_linux.sh -st -j 16 2>&1 | tee ~/build.log; echo BUILD_EXIT=$? >> ~/build.log' >/dev/null 2>&1 </dev/null &
```

Tests: `cd ~/JusPrin/build && DISPLAY=:99 ctest -C Release -j 8`.

## Sending new commits

```bash
git bundle create f.bundle jusprin-dev ^<commit the VM already has>
./vmscp.sh f.bundle VM:~/
./vmssh.sh 'cd ~/JusPrin && git pull ~/f.bundle jusprin-dev'
```

## Cost

The VM bills while running. Stop it when idle:

```bash
gcloud compute instances stop jusprin-linux-test --project elegoo-backend --zone us-west2-a
```

The external IP is ephemeral and changes on each start; the scripts look it up
by name, so nothing needs editing.
# Windows GUI test VM (GCP) — working harness

Drives a wxWidgets + OpenGL desktop app on a GPU-less Windows VM in GCP,
headlessly: launch it, screenshot it, click it, verify the result.

Verified 2026-09-07 with OrcaSlicer 2.4.2 portable.

## The VM

    instance : jusprin-win-test
    project  : elegoo-backend
    zone     : us-central1-a
    machine  : n2-standard-8, Windows Server 2022, 100GB pd-balanced
    display  : virtual display device ENABLED (required, see below)
    login    : ssh as guitest with ~/.ssh/google_compute_engine

The external IP is ephemeral and CHANGES on every stop/start. Re-read it with:

    gcloud compute instances describe jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a \
      --project=elegoo-backend \
      --format="value(networkInterfaces[0].accessConfigs[0].natIP)"

then update winssh.sh / winscp.sh.

## Four things that had to be solved

1. **OpenGL.** The app hard-requires OpenGL 3.2 (src/slic3r/GUI/OpenGLManager.cpp)
   and exits below it. Stock Windows software rendering reports 1.1. Fix: drop
   Mesa's `opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` (from pal1000/mesa-dist-win) next
   to the .exe. Reports OpenGL 4.2 on plain CPU.

   Mesa then auto-picks its **d3d12** backend, because the GCE virtual display
   exposes "Microsoft Basic Render Driver" as a D3D12 device — and that path
   crashed on the first frame. run-app.cmd forces the CPU rasterizer with
   `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`.

   Do NOT copy the whole Mesa .7z onto the VM: Windows Defender flags the archive
   as Trojan:Win32/Suschil!rfn and deletes it. Extract the two DLLs elsewhere and
   copy just those — Defender does not object to them, so no AV exclusion is
   needed. (The archive's sha256 matches GitHub's published release digest; the
   detection is a heuristic on the bundle, which also contains Vulkan layers,
   D3D12 compilers and media-foundation encoders we don't use.)

2. **A visible desktop.** A GUI app started from an SSH shell lands in a session
   with no desktop and screenshots come back black. autologon.ps1 creates a local
   admin `guitest` and sets Winlogon AutoAdminLogon so console session 1 is always
   live. Something in the GCE image clears those values after the boot that sets
   them, so startup.ps1 re-applies them on EVERY boot.

3. **Session isolation.** Display APIs, EnumWindows and Get-Process MainWindowTitle
   only see the CALLING session's window station. Run them over SSH and they
   silently report nothing — which reads as "the app has no window" when it does.
   Everything that touches the UI goes through `Invoke-InSession` in harness.ps1,
   which registers a scheduled task with `-LogonType Interactive` so it runs in
   session 1, and writes its output to a file to be read back over SSH.

4. **Resolution.** Without a GCE virtual display device the guest falls back to
   Microsoft Basic Display Adapter with no EDID = 640x480, and the app's own
   window is 760x500. Fix (requires the instance to be STOPPED):

       gcloud compute instances stop   jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend
       gcloud compute instances update jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend --enable-display-device
       gcloud compute instances start  jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend

   Then 1920x1080 is available via set-res.ps1.

## Also required by this app

Microsoft Edge WebView2 runtime is NOT present on a clean Windows Server image.
Without it the app puts up a modal "WebView2 Runtime" prompt and startup blocks
forever. Installed here as 152.0.4191.66 via the Evergreen bootstrapper:

    Invoke-WebRequest "https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/p/?LinkId=2124703" -OutFile setup.exe
    .\setup.exe /silent /install

This matters more for JusPrin than for stock Orca, since JusPrin's UI is
WebView-based.

## Files

    startup.ps1      GCE windows-startup-script-ps1: OpenSSH, port 22 firewall,
                     authorized_keys, calls autologon.ps1. Runs every boot.
    autologon.ps1    Creates guitest + sets AutoAdminLogon. Idempotent.
    harness.ps1      Invoke-InSession / Take-Screenshot. Source this first.
    screenshot.ps1   Screen capture. Must run in-session.
    probe.ps1        Lists session 1's real windows to C:\guitest\windows.txt.
    focus-app.ps1    Closes leftover task consoles, maximizes the app window.
    click.ps1        Clicks the "x,y" in C:\guitest\click.txt.
    set-res.ps1      Sets 1920x1080. Must run in-session.
    install-app.ps1  Downloads the app, places the Mesa DLLs beside the .exe.
    run-app.cmd      Launches the app with llvmpipe forced, detached.
    winssh.sh        ssh wrapper. winscp.sh: scp wrapper.

## Typical cycle

    ./winscp.sh <local.ps1> guitest@<IP>:C:/guitest/
    ./winssh.sh '. C:\guitest\harness.ps1; Invoke-InSession -TaskName "X" ...'
    ./winssh.sh '. C:\guitest\harness.ps1; Take-Screenshot'
    ./winscp.sh guitest@<IP>:C:/guitest/shot.png ./shot.png

## Known gap

There is no current JusPrin Windows binary to test. The Build all workflow's
Windows job fails at `cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022"` with "could not find any
instance of Visual Studio"; last green Windows build was 2026-03-04 and its
artifacts have expired. Either fix that job, or install VS Build Tools on this VM
and build from the cached OrcaSlicer_dep_win64 artifact.

**Run long builds as a SCHEDULED TASK, not over SSH.** Windows OpenSSH kills the
whole process tree when the session ends, so a build started from an SSH command
(even detached with Start-Process) dies on disconnect. Register it instead:

errors deep in Boost headers. Detect it with:
